note: The original describes only the first-form queen, with no alate or soldier; the caste heading follows the original as 'Other'.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Compound eyes smaller than in A. gracilis, and unlike that species it has a distinct fontanelle.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: First-form queen: head pale reddish chestnut, wider than long (from posterior margin to base of postclypeus), densely covered with long hairs. Fontanelle a transparent, nearly oval spot on the vertex. Postclypeus pale yellowish brown, slightly more than twice as wide as long, projecting, bilobed, with long hairs. Compound eyes black, nearly round, adjacent to the lateral margins of the head, projecting. Ocelli transparent, elongate-oval, separated from the compound eyes by about their long diameter, upper margin projecting, set obliquely to the compound eyes. Mandibles yellow with chestnut apices, elongate. Antennae yellowish brown, 15-segmented, gradually longer and wider toward the apex, with long hairs; segment 3 short, narrow, ring-like, shorter than segments 2 and 4; segment 4 slightly shorter than segment 2; apical segment slender, nearly oval. Pronotum pale yellowish brown, saddle-shaped, nearly cordate, posterior margin concave, with long hairs. Meso- and metanotum deeply and angularly incised. Legs pale yellow, with long hairs. Abdominal tergites yellowish brown with grey tinge, with faint spiracular spots, densely covered with long hairs; cerci indistinct. Measurements: queen body length 14.00 mm; head length (to the apex of the labrum) 1.00 mm; pronotum length 0.50 mm, width 0.75 mm; left mandible length 0.55 mm; hind tibia length 0.80 mm; compound eye long diameter 0.20 mm; queen abdomen width 2.00 mm; head width 0.85 mm. Type locality Rosario, Bolivia; a single first-form queen collected in November (month 11) by W. M. Mann together with workers; holotype first-form queen, USNM Cat. No. 27663.
